s: Who among the following was known as the ‘Frontier Gandhi’?
x: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was popularly known as the ‘Frontier Gandhi’ and was associated with the Khudai Khidmatgars.
tq: Use direct title–person recall.

s: Tanguturi Prakasam earned the title ‘Andhra Kesari’ in connection with which event?
o: The Quit India Movement in Andhra
The boycott of the Simon Commission at Madras
x: Tanguturi Prakasam became known as ‘Andhra Kesari’ for his prominent role in the Simon boycott at Madras.
tq: Link the title with the specific event associated with its conferment.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Deshbandhu was the title of C.R. Das. Lala Lajpat Rai was known as Punjab Kesari or the Lion of Punjab.
tq: Find the swapped personality–title pair.

s: Sarojini Naidu was popularly known as which of the following?
x: Sarojini Naidu was popularly known as Bharat Kokila, or the Nightingale of India.
tq: Test a well-known title through direct recall.

s: The title ‘Sardar’ was associated with Vallabhbhai Patel after which event?
x: Vallabhbhai Patel came to be known as ‘Sardar’ after his leadership in the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928.
tq: Use date-and-event discrimination for a title.

s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Punjab Kesari — Lala Lajpat Rai
2. Andhra Ratna — Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
3. Deshabhakta — Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
x: Lala Lajpat Rai was Punjab Kesari and Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was Andhra Ratna. Deshabhakta was Konda Venkatappayya, not Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
tq: Check each title–person pair before selecting the coded combination.

s: Who was known as ‘Desoddharaka’?
x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was known as ‘Desoddharaka’ and was the founder of Andhra Patrika.
tq: Distinguish closely related Andhra titles and personalities.

s:
With reference to the titles and associated personalities, consider the following statements:
1. Mannathu Padmanabhan was known as Bharatha Kesari.
2. Mannathu Padmanabhan founded the Nair Service Society.
3. He was associated with the Vaikom and Guruvayur Satyagrahas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Mannathu Padmanabhan was associated with the title Bharatha Kesari, founded the NSS and participated in the Vaikom and Guruvayur Satyagrahas.
tq: Use a cluster of biographical statements and verify all three links.

s: Who called Gandhi ‘Mahatma’?
x: Rabindranath Tagore is associated with calling Gandhi ‘Mahatma’.
tq: Test the originator of a famous honorific.

s: ‘The Golden Threshold’ is associated with which author?
x: ‘The Golden Threshold’ was written by Sarojini Naidu.
tq: Distinguish literary works by their authors.

s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. The Discovery of India — Jawaharlal Nehru
2. Annihilation of Caste — B.R. Ambedkar
3. Sarvodaya — Mahatma Gandhi
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
x: All three pairs are correct. The Discovery of India was written by Nehru, Annihilation of Caste by Ambedkar and Sarvodaya was Gandhi’s Gujarati rendering of Ruskin’s Unto This Last.
tq: Verify multiple work–author pairs and the associated literary source.

s: In which place was Jawaharlal Nehru’s ‘The Discovery of India’ written?
x: Jawaharlal Nehru wrote ‘The Discovery of India’ in Ahmednagar Fort jail.
tq: Test the place associated with a major work.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: A National Flag for India — Pingali
History of the Indian National Congress — Pattabhi
x: ‘Feathers and Stones’ was written by Pattabhi, not Sarojini Naidu. Gandhi wrote Hind Swaraj, while Pingali wrote A National Flag for India in 1916.
tq: Catch the swapped author in a list of familiar works.

s: ‘Sarvodaya’ is best described as which of the following?
o: A Hindi translation by Nehru of ‘The Discovery of India’
A collection of Ambedkar’s speeches on caste
A Gujarati rendering by Gandhi of John Ruskin’s ‘Unto This Last’
A Tamil translation of Gandhi’s prison songs
x: Gandhi’s ‘Sarvodaya’ is a Gujarati rendering of John Ruskin’s ‘Unto This Last’.
tq: Test the exact nature and source of a translated work.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Organisation)
a. Khaksars
b. Bal Charkha Sangh
c. Servants of the People Society
d. Independence for India League

List-II (Founder)
i. Jawaharlal Nehru
 ii. Indira Gandhi
 iii. Allama Inayatullah Khan Mashriqi
 iv. Lala Lajpat Rai

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Khaksars were founded by Allama Inayatullah Khan Mashriqi, Bal Charkha Sangh by Indira Gandhi, Servants of the People Society by Lala Lajpat Rai and the Independence for India League by Jawaharlal Nehru.
tq: Start from the sure founder–organisation pair and eliminate codes.

s: The Khaksars organisation was founded in which year?
x: Allama Inayatullah Khan Mashriqi founded the Khaksars in 1931.
tq: Use nearby-year discrimination among organisations.

s: Which organisation was founded by Lala Lajpat Rai?
x: Lala Lajpat Rai founded the Servants of the People Society.
tq: Distinguish organisations with similar names by their founders.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Harijan Sevak Sangh was founded in 1932.
2. It had branches at Hyderabad and Vijayawada.
3. Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was the president of its Vijayawada branch.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The Harijan Sevak Sangh was founded in 1932 and had branches at Hyderabad and Vijayawada, whose Vijayawada branch was headed by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
tq: Combine date, location and office-holder facts in one coded question.

s: From which saint did Gandhi take the term ‘Harijan’?
x: Gandhi took the term ‘Harijan’ from the saint Narsi Mehta.
tq: Test the source of a distinctive political-social term.

s:
Which of the following statements about Sarojini Naidu is correct?
1. She was associated with the Dharasana raid of 1930.
2. She became the first woman Governor of Uttar Pradesh.
3. She was associated with Hyderabad.
x: All three statements are correct. Sarojini Naidu was associated with Hyderabad, the Dharasana raid of 1930 and became the first woman Governor of Uttar Pradesh.
tq: Confirm a personality through region and multiple contributions.
sec: Women freedom fighters - region and contribution  [APPSC]

s: Durgabai Deshmukh stopped Jawaharlal Nehru without a pass at which place and event?
x: Durgabai Deshmukh stopped Nehru without a pass at the Vijayawada AICC meeting in 1921.
tq: Link a freedom fighter with a distinctive incident, place and year.
sec: Women freedom fighters - region and contribution  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Aruna Asaf Ali — Hoisting the flag at Gowalia Tank in 1942
Bhikaiji Cama — Quit India martyrdom at Tamluk
Durgabai Deshmukh — Translation of Gandhi’s Hindi speeches into Telugu
x: Bhikaiji Cama was associated with hoisting the Indian flag abroad at Stuttgart in 1907. Matangini Hazra was the Quit India martyr associated with Tamluk.
tq: Reject the mismatched contribution by comparing regional associations.
sec: Women freedom fighters - region and contribution  [APPSC]

s: Rani Gaidinliu joined the Heraka movement at approximately what age?
x: Rani Gaidinliu joined the Zeliangrong Heraka movement at the age of 13 and was jailed for about 14 years.
tq: Test a distinctive biographical number.
sec: Women freedom fighters - region and contribution  [APPSC]

s: Who gave Rani Gaidinliu the title ‘Rani’?
x: Jawaharlal Nehru called Gaidinliu ‘Rani’.
tq: Identify the person associated with a bestowed title.
sec: Women freedom fighters - region and contribution  [APPSC]

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Rani Velu Nachiyar wages war against the British
B. Bhikaiji Cama hoists the Indian flag at Stuttgart
C. Durgabai Deshmukh’s Vijayawada AICC incident
D. Aruna Asaf Ali hoists the flag at Gowalia Tank
x: The correct sequence is 1780, 1907, 1921 and 1942: Rani Velu Nachiyar, Bhikaiji Cama, Durgabai Deshmukh and Aruna Asaf Ali.
tq: Arrange events by their stated years, using the earliest event first.
sec: Women freedom fighters - region and contribution  [APPSC]

s: The statement, ‘Generations to come... will scarce believe that such a one... walked upon this earth’, was made by whom?
x: Albert Einstein made this statement in tribute to Mahatma Gandhi.
tq: Use quotation–speaker discrimination among prominent personalities.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gandhi described sedition as having become his religion.
2. Gandhi compared the Cripps offer to a post-dated cheque.
3. Subhas Chandra Bose compared the Dandi March with Napoleon’s return from Elba.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Gandhi made the first two observations, while Subhas Chandra Bose made the comparison concerning the Dandi March.
tq: Separate similar nationalist quotations by speaker and context.

s: V.O. Chidambaram Pillai founded which organisation?
x: V.O. Chidambaram Pillai founded the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company at Tuticorin.
tq: Match a leader with the organisation founded by him.

s: The Coral Mill strike of 1908 was associated with V.O. Chidambaram Pillai and which other leader?
x: V.O. Chidambaram Pillai participated in the 1908 Coral Mill strike along with Subramania Siva.
tq: Identify the associated co-participant in a specific movement.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: C. Rajagopalachari led the Vedaranyam Salt March. K. Kelappan was associated with Kerala, Gopinath Bordoloi with Assam and Kesari Singh Barahath with Rajasthan.
tq: Use region–leader–movement association to eliminate mismatches.

s: Who was known as the ‘Kerala Gandhi’?
x: K. Kelappan of Kerala was popularly known as the ‘Kerala Gandhi’ and was associated with the Guruvayur Satyagraha.
tq: Test a regional honorific and its associated movement.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Lala Lajpat Rai was associated with Punjab.
2. He was a member of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio.
3. He presided over the Indian National Congress in 1920.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Lala Lajpat Rai belonged to Punjab, formed part of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio and presided over the Congress in 1920.
tq: Combine region, political association and office held.

s: Gopinath Bordoloi is best associated with which of the following descriptions?
o: Leader of the Guruvayur Satyagraha in Kerala
Poet and revolutionary of Shahpura in Rajasthan
Builder of modern Assam who was jailed in 1941 and 1942
Founder of the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company in Tamil Nadu
x: Gopinath Bordoloi was regarded as a builder of modern Assam and was jailed in 1941 and 1942.
tq: Identify the correct regional biography from closely related alternatives.

s: Kesari Singh Barahath was associated with which region and role?
x: Kesari Singh Barahath belonged to Shahpura in Rajasthan and was known as a poet and revolutionary.
tq: Match region with identity and contribution.

s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes Subramania Siva?
1. He belonged to Tamil Nadu.
2. He was the first political prisoner of the Madras Presidency.
3. He worked with V.O. Chidambaram Pillai and Subramania Bharati.
x: All three statements are correct. Subramania Siva was from Tamil Nadu, regarded as the first political prisoner of the Madras Presidency, and worked with VOC and Bharati.
tq: Confirm a lesser-known personality through three linked facts.

s: Who presided over the Indian National Congress session held at Calcutta in 1917?
x: Annie Besant presided over the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1917.
tq: Match the leader with the correct Congress session and year.

s: Lajpat Rai presided over which session of the Indian National Congress?
x: Lajpat Rai presided over the special session of the Congress held at Calcutta in 1920.
tq: Discriminate between closely placed Congress sessions.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I — Congress President

a. Mahatma Gandhi
b. Sarojini Naidu
c. M.A. Ansari
 d. Jawaharlal Nehru

List-II — Session and year

i. Lahore, 1929
 ii. Belgaum, 1924
 iii. Kanpur, 1925
 iv. Madras, 1927

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Gandhi presided at Belgaum in 1924, Sarojini Naidu at Kanpur in 1925, M.A. Ansari at Madras in 1927 and Nehru at Lahore in 1929.
tq: Start from the sure leader–session pair and eliminate the codes.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Congress presidencies:
1. Subhas Chandra Bose presided over the Haripura session in 1938.
2. Subhas Chandra Bose presided over the Tripuri session in 1939.
3. Rajendra Prasad became Congress President in 1939 after Bose.
4. Mahatma Gandhi presided over the Lahore session of 1929.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the Lahore session of 1929 was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru.
tq: Find the wrong president–session association.

s: The National Liberal Federation was formed by moderates who had left the Congress during which period?
x: The National Liberal Federation was formed by moderates who left the Congress during 1918–19.
tq: Use the period as the deciding numerical clue.

s: Who is associated with the National Liberal Federation as its leading figure at the time of its formation?
x: Surendranath Banerjee was associated with the National Liberal Federation formed by moderates who had left the Congress.
tq: Separate the founding association from later presidents.

s:
Which of the following persons were among the presidents of the National Liberal Federation?
1. Tej Bahadur Sapru
2. V.S. Srinivasa Sastri
3. Surendranath Banerjee
4. Subhas Chandra Bose

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Tej Bahadur Sapru and V.S. Srinivasa Sastri were among the presidents of the National Liberal Federation. Surendranath Banerjee was associated with its formation, while Bose was not listed as its president.
tq: Distinguish the organisation’s presidents from its associated founder figure.

s:
Tanguturi Prakasam is associated with which of the following contributions?
1. Participation in the Simon boycott in Madras
2. Salt Satyagraha at Devarampadu
3. Becoming the first Chief Minister of Andhra State in 1953
4. Designing the national flag

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Prakasam participated in the Simon boycott in Madras, led the salt satyagraha at Devarampadu and became the first Chief Minister of Andhra State in 1953. Flag design is associated with Pingali Venkayya.
tq: Identify the one contribution belonging to another Andhra leader.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pattabhi Sitaramayya — First Chief Minister of Andhra State, 1953
x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya was associated with Andhra Bank, Andhra Insurance and the JVP Committee. Tanguturi Prakasam, not Pattabhi Sitaramayya, was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State in 1953.
tq: Find the swapped leader–achievement pair.

s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya lost the contest for Congress President at which session?
x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya lost the contest for Congress President at the Tripuri session in 1939.
tq: Use the close year and session distinction.

s: Who was known by the title ‘Deshabhakta’ and served as the dictator of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha?
x: Konda Venkatappayya was known as ‘Deshabhakta’ and was the dictator of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha.
tq: Match the title and organisational role with the correct leader.

s:
Consider the following statements about Pingali Venkayya:
1. He was born at Bhatlapenumarru.
2. His flag design was endorsed by Gandhi at Vijayawada in 1921.
3. He was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Pingali Venkayya was born at Bhatlapenumarru and his flag design was endorsed by Gandhi at Vijayawada in 1921. The first Chief Minister of Andhra State was Tanguturi Prakasam.
tq: Reject the office wrongly attributed to the flag designer.

s: The flag adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947 differed from the earlier design mainly because the Ashoka Chakra replaced the:
x: The Constituent Assembly adopted the present national flag on 22 July 1947, with the Ashoka Chakra replacing the charkha.
tq: Test the precise change in a familiar symbol.

s: Potti Sriramulu undertook a fast unto death primarily for the formation of:
x: Potti Sriramulu undertook a fast unto death for the formation of Andhra State.
tq: Identify the specific political demand behind the fast.

s:
Consider the following statements about Potti Sriramulu:
1. He died on 15 December 1952.
2. His fast lasted for 58 days.
3. His fast was connected with the demand for Andhra State.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct: Potti Sriramulu died on 15 December 1952 after a 58-day fast undertaken for Andhra State.
tq: Combine date, duration and objective in one statement set.

s: The Rampa rebellion led by Alluri Sitarama Raju was directed against conditions associated with which legislation and practice?
o: Madras Forest Act of 1882 and forced labour
Government of India Act of 1935 and zamindari
Indian Councils Act of 1909 and indentured labour
Forest Rights Act of 2006 and bonded labour
x: The Rampa rebellion of 1922–24 was connected with opposition to the Madras Forest Act of 1882 and forced labour.
tq: Connect the movement with its immediate causes rather than its leader alone.

s: The Andhra kisan movement and the Andhra Socialist Party were associated with:
x: N.G. Ranga was associated with the Andhra kisan movement and the Andhra Socialist Party; he also resigned his professorship in 1930.
tq: Match the regional organisation and movement with its leader.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I — Leader

a. Birsa Munda
b. Alluri Sitarama Raju
c. Komaram Bheem
 d. Swami Sahajanand Saraswati

List-II — Organisation or movement

i. Bihar Kisan Sabha
 ii. Munda Ulgulan
 iii. Gond movement
 iv. Rampa movement

s: The Munda Ulgulan was associated with which leader and region?
x: Birsa Munda led the Munda Ulgulan in the Chotanagpur region.

s: Komaram Bheem is associated with which movement and slogan?
o: Bihar Kisan Sabha — ‘Swaraj is my birthright’
x: Komaram Bheem was associated with the Gond movement during 1938–44 and with the slogan ‘Jal-Jangal-Zameen’.
tq: Use the distinctive slogan to identify the movement and leader.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the tribal movements is correct?
o: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa movement among Koya and Jatapu tribals.
Birsa Munda led the Gond movement in 1938–44.
Komaram Bheem led the Munda Ulgulan in Chotanagpur.
Swami Sahajanand Saraswati led the Rampa movement in Andhra.
x: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa movement among the Koya and Jatapu tribals. The other statements interchange the leaders and movements.

s: In August 2026, the Prime Minister marked which occasion associated with Pingali Venkayya?
o: The centenary of the Constituent Assembly
x: The Prime Minister marked Pingali Venkayya’s 150th birth anniversary in August 2026.
tq: Identify the correct anniversary figure from the current-affairs options.

s: Events marking the 154th anniversary of Tanguturi Prakasam were held in August 2026 at:
x: Events marking Tanguturi Prakasam’s 154th anniversary were held at Visakhapatnam and Ongole in August 2026.
tq: Use the paired locations as the decisive clue.

s: Who unveiled Rajaji’s bust at Rashtrapati Bhavan during Rajaji Utsav in February 2026?
o: The Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu
x: The President unveiled Rajaji’s bust at Rashtrapati Bhavan during Rajaji Utsav in February 2026.
tq: Apply the ‘who would perform this official act?’ method.

s: A Guinness record involving more than 13,000 tribal women performing Dhimsa was associated with which place?
o: Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Bhogapuram
x: The Dhimsa Guinness record involving more than 13,000 tribal women was achieved at the new Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram.
tq: Combine the event, scale and location instead of relying on the name alone.

s: On the 80th Independence Day, the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh recalled which two leaders?
o: Alluri Sitarama Raju and Pingali Venkayya
x: The Chief Minister recalled Alluri Sitarama Raju and Pingali Venkayya on the 80th Independence Day.
tq: Identify the correct commemorative pair.

s: Which of the following comparative statements is correct regarding the national presence of leaders?
o: Prakasam and Rajaji were the only leaders with an all-India political role.
Rajaji, Prakasam and EMS had greater national presence than Gandhi, Nehru, Bose and Patel.
Southern leaders such as Rajaji, Prakasam and EMS had less national presence than Gandhi, Nehru, Bose and Patel.
Only EMS had a national presence, whereas Gandhi and Nehru were regional leaders.
x: The comparative assessment is that southern leaders such as Rajaji, Prakasam and EMS had less national presence than Gandhi, Nehru, Bose and Patel.
tq: Test the direction of the comparison and reject its reversal.
